symptom: `mxcli check` passes and `exec` prints `Created association`, then the project no longer OPENS — `KeyNotFoundException … at StreamingBsonUnitReader.ResolvePostponedProperties()`, a stack trace naming no document
cause: An association whose FROM entity lives in ANOTHER module. Mendix stores an association in the module of its FROM entity, so a remote FROM writes a `ParentPointer` aimed at an element in a different unit. Not a build error — a LOAD error, so Studio Pro cannot open it either
insight: **Refuse; there is nothing to write instead.** Neither stored form can express it: `DomainModels$Association` holds two element IDs both local to the unit, and `DomainModels$CrossAssociation` holds a local `ParentPointer` plus a BY_NAME `ChildRef` — there is no by-name PARENT. Check the storage shape before treating a direction as a writer bug. The reported case was `from System.User`, but it is **not System-specific** — `from Administration.Account` fails identically, and a guard keyed on System would pass the general case through; the rule is the module boundary. Control both ways: the supported direction (`from MyModule.X to System.User`) and a plain same-module association must stay at 0 errors, and stubbing the guard must bring the KeyNotFoundException back. To locate a dangling GUID at all, scan every `.mxunit` for the raw 16 bytes in BOTH endiannesses (`uuid.bytes` and `uuid.bytes_le` — little-endian is the one that hits). **Run `make check-mdl` before pushing any new `mdl-examples/` file**: CI runs every example as a POSITIVE test unless it is named `*.fail.mdl`, so a fixture demonstrating a refusal fails the build. Split it — refused statements in the `.fail.mdl`, working forms in a sibling `.mdl`, each pointing at the other — so both halves are actually gated rather than only the negative one. ako/mxcli-captrack
